title: UFOs seen by Oil Rig Worker in Gulf of Mexico
excerpt: This video is getting some exposure on X. Source: https://x.com/Jehoseph/status/2120076265780920457?a=J978X_2Yoh4eK0EZGIo&s=19 Date and Time is unknown, but presumably this was recently. The location was given as on an oil rig 100miles offshore from Alabama...
content:
• #3

I've tried to match the stars in the video with known stars, looking west has a better match but its not conclusive.

"Sent this in the middle of the night" works well for the 3AM eastward flares

  • #4

"Sent this in the middle of the night" works well for the 3AM eastward flares

Although... to be SENT in the middle of the night, it would have to have been taken earlier?

  • #5

There will be wifi on the rig so no reason it couldn't be sent just after being taken

  • #6

There will be wifi on the rig so no reason it couldn't be sent just after being taken

Maybe, but would AFTER 3 am be described as the middle of the night? There seems to me to be a larger window of "middle of the night" after an evening sighting than a morning one.

Not saying it could not have been the morning show that was videoed, just that I don't think being sent "in the middle of the night" really favors one interpretation over the other.

With the added possibility that the poster could be in a different time zone (I walked through several layers of subreddits trying to see if I could find any mention of where the poster was located, and gave up, perhaps somebody else knows how to find that, or has already found it?) So "middle of the night" may refer to when it was received, in which case it tells us nothing about when it was sent unless we know where the poster was located, time-zone-wise.

  • #7

12-4am is the colloquial 'middle of the night' to me

As happens often we are with no details, with details this one would have recreated by me, Mick or Flarkey as soon as we found out about it, thus potentially nipping it in the bud.
